FAQ.heading: FAQs
FAQ.subheading: Everything you might wonder about splitting expenses without servers, accounts or the cloud.
FAQ.stillDesc: Our community of contributors is happy to help you out.

whatIs.a: Zplit is an open-source mobile app for splitting group expenses. Unlike other expense-sharing apps, it is fully decentralized: there are no servers, no cloud and no accounts. Your data lives on your device and syncs directly with your friends' devices.

noServers.q: How does Zplit work without servers?
noServers.a: Zplit uses peer-to-peer technologies like WiFi Direct, Bluetooth and NFC to sync data directly between devices. All your expense data is stored locally on your device with encryption. When you're near friends, devices sync changes with each other.

notNearby.q: What if I'm not near my friends?
notNearby.a: You can share groups and expenses via QR codes or deep links that work over any messaging app. The data syncs when the code is scanned or the link is opened. You can also export encrypted backups and share them manually.

offline.q: Does Zplit need an internet connection?
offline.a: No. Zplit is offline-first, so you can create groups, add expenses and check balances with no connection at all, whether you're on a mountain trek or a flight. Everything syncs once your devices meet again.

secure.a: Yes. All data is encrypted and stored only on your device. There are no Zplit servers, so there is no central database to breach. Peer-to-peer transfers are end-to-end encrypted, and you stay in full control of your data.

account.q: Do I need to create an account?
account.a: No. There are no sign-ups, emails or phone numbers. Just create a group and invite friends by QR code, NFC, Bluetooth or WiFi.

splits.q: How can I split an expense?
splits.a: Split any expense equally, by percentage or by custom amounts. Zplit calculates balances in real time so everyone can see who owes whom, and you can filter expenses by date, category or member.

ocr.a: Point your camera at a receipt and Zplit extracts the merchant name, amount and date using on-device machine learning (Google ML Kit). The image is processed locally and never uploaded anywhere.

platforms.a: Zplit is available on Android through Google Play. It is built with Flutter, a single cross-platform codebase that also targets iOS.

openSource.q: Is Zplit free and open source?
openSource.a: Yes. Zplit is free and 100% open source, developed in the open under AOSSIE. You can read, audit and build every line of code yourself from GitHub.

contribute.a: Head to the Zplit repository on GitHub, pick an issue or propose a feature, and open a pull request. Bug reports and ideas are just as welcome. Say hello on Discord to get started.
